lens: A — Constitution & Gate 0 (10 invariants, Gate-0 exit criteria, one-kernel discipline)

recommendations.action: Owner declares ONE trunk (work/g0-trunk-20260817, plan revision 6) and freezes checkpoint/2026-07-20-session to read-only harvest status. Reconcile the constitutional fork explicitly: replay this line's amendment 003 (serena-first) as a new record on the trunk chain, and append a reconciliation record stating which chain is authoritative. Whichever way each door goes, blocker-ize or amend the closed predicate so LOCAL_GUARDS/non-CENTRAL rows cannot silently satisfy 'centralized start/guard path'.

Owner decision 2: pick the sealed-approval trust root. Evidence favors option B (asymmetric git-signed tag): port this line's spine/promotion_approval.py verifier onto the trunk promotion path, add the approval parameter to promote_candidates, construct PromotionReceipt, and either retire the symmetric HMAC path or demote it to a ledgered second factor with the divergence recorded. Touches protected promotion policy.

Convert the 6 declared-blocked fault-matrix lines to measured lines by running them on a Linux host/CI, and state the security boundary honestly at stamp time: win32 MIC write-bounded containment with CONFIDENTIALITY: NONE, not a sandbox. Fix the v3 duplicate-callsite scanner crash first so repository-write evidence is obtainable, and add SECRETS rows to the registry before closing (Invariant 8).

Re-run the census on the trunk at 93f11adf before spending on ANY module-level fix from this council's inventory; produce a harvest list of checkpoint-line assets to port via the established blob-port lane pattern (candidates verified valuable: tools/vet gate hardening + its 207 test lines, structcore gardener distillates G-01/G-02, promotion_approval verifier, amendment-003 hook).

Propose a guard change: match protected-artifact enforcement on write intent, not on literal path substrings in read-only tool payloads, so inventories and councils can name what they audited. Until then, publish the sanctioned path-decoder convention used by slices 7/10 so evidence is non-literal but decodable (protects Invariant 7).

Gate-1 ignition strictly after the stamp: rehearsal green + G1 activation checklist, using the trunk's MissionContract path (not this line's legacy AgentTask/BuildSession vocabulary). Reconcile build.py's BuildSession/Wave with MissionContract->WorkItems->Attempts as part of the ignition slice, not before.

Isolated experiments stay where they are: runs/higher_twin_nc and experiments/forest_v2 are correctly filed and labeled; add the one missing mechanical control — an experiment registry with expiry checks (higher_twin_nc declares Expiry 2026-10-31 but nothing enforces it) — wired through the canonical kernel, not a new subsystem.

dissent: Against the likely majority ranking: the module islands this council inventoried (unconsumed canonical contracts, INVENTORY_ONLY registry rows, unwired promotion verifier) are NOT the Gate-0 critical path. They are measurements of a line 1,228 commits behind the closure work; on the trunk the blocker list is 20 named lines and two owner decisions. Spending council-driven lanes on wiring THIS tree is token burn on a frozen line — harvest and port instead.
Against calling forest_v2-on-trunk a gate-order violation: it is filed under experiments/ with tests, which section 10 explicitly permits. The violation is the fork, not the prototyping.

Against treating the guard's read-only misfires as acceptable strictness: three misfires in one read-only session is a measured defect, and its practical effect (agents obfuscating paths in evidence) is anti-provenance — worse than the marginal protection gained.
Against 'delete the shims now' as priority hygiene: deletions on a frozen line are churn that widens the diff the port has to reason about. Delete only on the surviving trunk.

Partial dissent from the owner memory's framing that exactly two owner decisions remain: the exit-delta adds three honesty gaps (SECRETS unmodeled, closed-predicate weaker than plan text, v3 scanner crash) that are not owner decisions but must land before a stamp is honest — otherwise closed:true asserts things the report cannot see.
for_codex: The repo holds two amendment chains rooted at the same revision-1 sha (checkpoint: rev 2, accepted 2026-08-21; trunk: rev 6, 2026-08-02). Under section 15, what is the legal reconciliation that is not a history rewrite — and can a plan legitimately claim 'sole semantic authority' during the interval when two adopted revisions coexist? Attack my AMENDMENT-now recommendation if you think a pure ALIGNED merge-of-records suffices.

Is the trunk's symmetric HMAC owner-approval (secret in an environment variable, approvals.py:732/767) compatible with Invariants 3+5 at all, given any process that reads that env can mint a verifying approval? Or is 'depends on whether a candidate ever sees the var' (the conflict doc's hedge) an acceptable residual for a Gate-0 stamp?

The gate report's closed predicate (report.py:203-209) tolerates 11 LOCAL_GUARDS rows never reaching CENTRAL, and 0/53 rows model SECRETS. Argue whether closing Gate 0 on that predicate falsifies the plan's own exit text — or whether blocker-izing everything makes the gate unreachable and the plan text should be amended instead.

Can a fault-injection matrix 'demonstrate fail-closed' when 6 of 24 lines are declared-blocked-with-reason rather than executed (Docker scoping + live envelope)? Define the minimum evidence standard under which the 24/24 signed claim is honest, and what the Linux CI run must show.

Attack the staleness thesis itself: enumerate which of this council's ten-slice findings SURVIVE on the trunk at 93f11adf (two capability vocabularies? conversation.py fourth log? loop.py unregistered door? vet gate unwired?). Any finding that survives the port is real; any that doesn't was audit-of-a-ghost. What is the cheapest census that answers this?

Is a workflow guard that rejects read-only payloads for containing protected path literals a net safety positive or negative, given the measured effect (agents writing path decoders to smuggle evidence past it)? Propose the narrowest match rule that still blocks actual writes.

lens: B — Research direction: tensor embeddings + category theory pivot (schizo check against the repo's own measurement discipline)
headline: The categorical strand already runs as the repo's best experiment — embedding-free, pre-registered, killed-criteria'd; the tensor pivot is honest in exactly two forms: (1) the ceiling classification that was written 2026-07-30 and never run, and (2) an operator-embedding K-predictor supervised by higher_twin_nc's interventional commutators — everything else is occupied literature (RESCAL/TuckER, DisCoCat/TPR, Hansen–Ghrist sheaves) or word salad the plan already bans.

recommendations.action: Run the latent ceiling classification exactly as pre-registered (LATENT_CEILING_SHARED_REPRESENTATION.md sec.2-4): classify the on-disk failure corpus into (a) covered-by-brief / (b) present-but-not-expressible / (c) absent, respecting the sec.5 sequencing rule (never concurrent with gate_discrimination). This is the gate for EVERY latent proposal, tensor or flat. Pre-register the tensor-go threshold before the run (e.g. bucket-(b) >= 15%).

Write the novelty-narrowing table for the tensor pivot BEFORE any code, in the LAYER2 sec.2 style: multi-relational factorization = RESCAL/DistMult/ComplEx/TuckER/RotatE; non-commutative compositional embeddings = Smolensky TPR, Rudolph-Giesbrecht CMSM, DisCoCat (Coecke-Sadrzadeh-Clark); vector-stalk descent = Hansen-Ghrist cellular sheaves / sheaf NNs (Bodnar); code-graph embeddings = code2vec, GraphCodeBERT, CodexGraph/RepoGraph/LocAgent. Every categorical term must name its operational cash-out (what is the tensor-product of two Node Cards, measured how) or be struck.

Build the history-replay corpus with per-model contamination attest (already SPEC backlog, runs/higher_twin_nc/SPEC.md:332-338). It is the shared critical path: higher_twin_nc's confirmation phase AND any learned-representation claim are both untestable without it. Corpus-building, not tensor math, is where the next research unit of spend belongs.

Register operator-embedding K-prediction as a NEW frozen ExperimentSpec (do not fold into higher_twin_nc's alpha family): fit per-operator matrices (or low-rank tensors) to predict continuous K_behave on held-out pairs, supervised by the existing anchor-verified kmatrix receipts. Mandatory baselines: (a) always-zero additive model, (b) declared-footprint overlap, (c) measured-footprint overlap, (d) co-change, (e) the strongest FLAT baseline — embed the composed diff texts AB vs BA directly and use their distance. Kill: no advantage over measured-footprint overlap; or predictions reduce to the certificate (only fires where footprints overlap); or fitted matrices are gauge-unidentifiable (pass-31 hazard). Calibration-only until the history-replay corpus exists.

Plane-mode-structured embedding ablation (Tucker core / mode-tagged Node Cards vs flat concatenation under equal dimension and token budget), judged by the existing eval harness (eval/graph_delta.py --held-out fitness). Blocked on the ceiling run reporting bucket-(b) above the pre-registered threshold; expect the hub measurement to cap the useful rank. Kill: no gain over flat concat at equal budget, per Gate-2 ablation rules.

Vector-stalk sheaf over the footprint site (the 'tensorized descent' idea) only if descent-at-scale produces obstruction-localization failures the digest-level gluing assays cannot address; the spec must name Hansen-Ghrist as occupied territory and state why the sealed-evaluator constraint (behavior observable only via assay calls) does not make spectral methods inapplicable. Suspect answer today: it does; refuse until shown otherwise.

Refuse, now and explicitly, any elevation of a tensor/latent space to canonical status (a fifth plane, a universal coordinate system, an embedding-gated promotion) — that would require an owner-approved AMENDMENT against Invariant 4 and section 12, and is premature until the ceiling, corpus, and K-predictor experiments have reported. Record the refusal so the pivot pressure has a named answer.

Keep higher_twin_nc's next spend on the external-fixture confirmation phase, not on a fifth author fixture: by the repo's own Messkonstruktionsregel (SPEC.md:108-113), instrument-polishing on author fixtures can never become an effect claim, and the expiry clock (2026-10-31, SPEC.md:8) is running with nothing mechanical checking it.

dissent: Against the expected kernel-councillor line 'freeze all research until Gate 0 exits': the ceiling classification is read-only, cheap, pre-registered by the repo itself, and the plan explicitly permits read-only critique and isolated experiments during Gate 0. Blocking a one-pass measurement behind kernel wiring wastes the repo's strongest asset — its measurement discipline — and higher_twin_nc proves the isolated-experiment pattern works under Gate 0.

Against the owner's pivot framing itself: the categorical strand does NOT need tensors or embeddings to progress — its embedding-freeness is why it survived adversarial review (Momus/Refuter/Codex) intact. Fusing a learned representation INTO higher_twin_nc would corrupt the one exemplary experiment; tensors should CONSUME its receipts as supervision in a separate frozen spec, never co-evolve with it (forbidden co-evolution, plan sec.8/12).

Against latent-infrastructure enthusiasm generally: the honest prior is a LOW ceiling. The ceiling doc's own recorded prediction is that most failures land in bucket (a) because 'the graph already knows' (LATENT_CEILING:83-93), semantic_route measured 0/5 production use, and the biggest measured win of the whole research program (graph_brief, daedalus/lanes/graph_brief.py:3-17) was deterministic text, not vectors.

Mild dissent against higher_twin_nc's own momentum: six watchdog slices in one day, all on author fixtures, is instrument calibration compounding — impressive engineering, zero effect-claim progress by the experiment's own rules. The council should not read '63/63 green' as research advance; only the external corpus can produce a finding.
for_codex: Attack the falsification argument in finding 3: a flat embedding of whole-tree STATES with a nonlinear readout can represent order effects; only intervention-as-vector-offset models are structurally commutative. Is baseline (e) — embed the composed diff texts AB vs BA and use their distance — already sufficient to predict K_behave, making the operator-matrix experiment redundant before it starts?

Power analysis: with ~40 measured pairs across 4 author fixtures and severe class imbalance (chemlab all-zero by construction, textlab behavior-neutral), can ANY learned K-predictor be statistically distinguished from the measured-footprint-overlap heuristic? Compute the minimum corpus size before the spec is registered — if it exceeds what history-replay can plausibly deliver by expiry, the experiment is dead on arrival.

Gauge freedom: LAYER2 pass 31 rejected learned-matrix commutator norms as basis-dependent. Does the same argument contaminate the K-predictor even when scored against interventional ground truth (fitted W_A, W_B unidentifiable up to conjugation, so ||[W_A,W_B]|| is not a stable feature)? Is there a gauge-invariant parameterization — e.g., predicting K only through evaluator-space observables — and if not, is the experiment ill-posed?

Is higher_twin_nc's descent machinery formally a cellular sheaf with 0-dimensional (digest-valued) stalks over the footprint site? If yes, does Hansen-Ghrist spectral obstruction theory give a cheaper localizer than gluing assays — or does the sealed evaluator (behavior observable ONLY via budgeted assay calls, no gradient, no spectrum) make the entire sheaf-Laplacian toolbox inapplicable? Name the exact obstruction.

Contamination firewall: nomic-embed-text's training corpus is undisclosed. Can a contamination attest (model cutoff vs repo timestamp, required by SPEC.md:110-113 and the two-judge expedition) be produced for ANY off-the-shelf embedding backbone on public-repo history-replay data — or does the firewall rule out every pretrained embedding for K-prediction, forcing from-scratch features and changing the cost calculus entirely?

Does the hub measurement (top-8 types = 83.6% of edges; post-cap plane near tree-like at 2599 edges/2067 nodes) bound the useful rank of any Tucker/mode-structured factorization over the four planes to something trivially small — i.e., is the 'tensor structure' of this repo's Twin empirically indistinguishable from a handful of stopword dimensions plus a sparse remainder that BM25 already captures?

recommendations.action: NOW / Serena availability: owner lands MCP_TIMEOUT (>=60000, value copied from claude-serena-watchdog.ps1:404-405) in the tracked project settings env block and adds a Serena prewarm step to the session launcher, so the cold start never races the timeout on a fresh checkout. Owner-run because the settings file is a protected artifact (harness guard-edit boundary); the diff is one env line, prepared for the owner as a snippet in the proposals island.

NOW / the ONE wiring for structcore adoption: add a `daedalus brief <paths>` CLI subcommand wrapping daedalus/lanes/graph_brief.graph_brief (read-only, registered in the effect registry so it is not another unregistered door), plus a thin repo skill instructing the crew to run it before any write-touching work. Chosen over a hook (hook install is owner-gated in protected settings and the proposals island has been pending since 2026-08-17 — a wiring that waits on the owner's calendar has measured adoption of zero) and over an MCP server (a second long-running server recreates the exact cold-start race that killed Serena adoption, and the index has no warm process — index.py:1179 in-process cache, clone clustering ~96% of build cost per ignore.py:22-27).

NOW / measure adoption instead of asserting it: serena-first.py is already the choke point — have it append one JSONL line per decision (deny / pass / inert-because-Serena-down) under runs/, and count `daedalus brief` invocations from transcripts. Adoption criteria, pre-registered with dynamic range per the measurement rules: (a) hook-inert sessions <5% over 2 weeks (current value unknown — that is itself the finding); (b) >=1 brief call in >50% of write-touching sessions within 2 weeks of the skill landing; (c) zero recurrences of the hallucinated-symbol class in gated writes (symbol-survival guard logs); (d) kill criterion: if brief+Serena does not reduce tokens-per-verified-gate-passing-write vs a grep baseline over N>=20 tasks, drop the mandate.

NEXT / install arch_hook.py per-turn delta injection via the sanctioned owner-run recovery-kit path (it is already present in docs/recovery/settings_beast.json), measuring token cost per turn before/after — this supersedes part of the brief skill once live, and the two share the freshness-first discipline (arch_memory.py:15-17).

NEXT / close the embedding egress gap before any new embedding consumer: route the Ollama embedding backend's host through the sensitivity lane check (lane_for_host) like every other lane, and record a post-fix live-probe measurement for semantic_route (the 0/5 finding has a fix but no re-measurement — its production status is currently unmeasured, not fixed).

NEXT / minimal embedding index over daedalus/ ONLY as a registered isolated experiment with SPEC (budget, expiry, kill criteria, sealed evaluation): frozen query set drawn from real crew retrieval needs, budget-equal comparison against graph_brief+Serena and against plain grep/BM25, pre-registered precision threshold. Mechanical cost is small (~local Ollama, minutes of GPU, infra already exists in the 1687-line store) — the enable is what is unproven, and section 13's kill criteria (full representation must beat BM25/code-only) apply verbatim.

LATER / persist the structcore index as a warm artifact (the missing piece named in the structcore slice: no persisted index, every CLI call re-folds, clone clustering ~96% of the time) so brief calls become sub-second; this is the precondition for ever revisiting an MCP-server-over-structcore, not the other way round.

LATER / docs hygiene: stamp v-embeddings.md as superseded-by-fix with the closing commit reference, and add the post-fix status line to semantic_route.py's measurement comment — stale verification records are the doc-drift defect class this repo hunts, sitting in its own verification directory.

dissent: Against the expected 'build an MCP server over structcore' consensus: a second in-repo MCP server is the wrong move at current maturity — it recreates the 28s-vs-30s cold-start race that already killed Serena adoption, adds an unregistered long-running process during Gate 0, and blocks on the warm-index work anyway. CLI subcommand + skill gets measurable adoption this week without touching protected settings.

Against the owner's own framing: 'the crew underuses semantic retrieval' is, on this repo's evidence, actually 'the crew underuses STRUCTURAL retrieval'. Every latent artifact measured here underperformed or never ran (semantic_route 0/5 live probes, A2 ceiling 2.3%, freshness unanchored), while the measured failure class (hallucinated symbol names, unseen function-body import edges) is answered exactly by graph_brief and Serena. Conflating the two would spend a lane on the weaker prior.

Against treating serena-first's fail-open as adequate: fail-open without a counter is silent drift by construction — the exact vocabulary the iron plan uses. The hook's design is right (amendment proposal 002 point B), but shipping it without an inert-rate measurement means nobody can say whether the mandatory-Serena policy has ever been in force for a majority of sessions. I expect others to call this fine; I call it a guard-honesty defect.

Against 'install the hook first' (likely from the harness-lens councillor): arch_hook is the better end state but is owner-gated behind protected settings, and the proposals island shows owner-gated harness changes sit for days-to-weeks. Sequencing the crew-reachable CLI+skill first is the difference between measured adoption in two weeks and another built-but-inert artifact — the repo's most common failure mode (graph built, measured, never connected to the consumer: graph_brief.py:16).

Partial dissent on Gate-4 hygiene: making brief+Serena the crew default quietly turns every crew session into a graph-conditioned arm with no control, which could contaminate the later Gate 4 comparison (graph-conditioned representation search vs retrieval baselines). I still recommend it — product reliability now outweighs a research-design convenience — but the council should log it as a known confound rather than discover it at Gate 4.
for_codex: serena-first.py proves Serena liveness by probing the dashboard port (127.0.0.1:24282, 0.15s timeout) because 'the MCP transport itself is not observable from a hook' (serena-first.py:39-44). Attack this proxy: can Serena be half-up — dashboard listening, LSP backend dead or still indexing — so the hook DENIES the Read fallback while Serena cannot actually answer, inverting the fail-open guarantee exactly when it matters?

graph_brief's 12k-char default budget was sized from this repo's symbol layer at 6,479 chars (graph_brief.py:55-59), and the ollama lane sheds the brief FIRST on overflow (ollama.py:822-827). Is prepend-and-shed-first the right priority order, and does truncation-honesty actually survive on a repo 10x this size — or does the brief degrade into exactly the 'quietly stops listing files' hallucination source it was written to prevent?

If brief+Serena becomes the crew default, every future crew-produced result is graph-conditioned with no control arm. Does this contaminate the Gate 4 protocol (graph-conditioned representation search vs budget-equal retrieval baselines), and what is the minimal pre-registration NOW — e.g. logging brief-bytes-injected per task — that keeps the later comparison honest?

The embedding store's identity anchor is trust-on-first-use (embeddings.py:48-53): an index written before anchoring ADOPTS an existing projection as its anchor. Attack the adoption path: can a poisoned or wrong-host first write silently define the coordinate system that all later drift detection then confirms as 'correct'?

Is tokens-per-verified-gate-passing-write a gameable adoption metric (agents steering toward smaller writes, or the gate itself moving), and what would a non-gameable retrieval-value measurement look like given this repo's measurement-construction rules — author of the question must not author the answer, dynamic range before any number?

The watchdog sets MCP_TIMEOUT=60000 (ps1:404-405) while the local overlay reportedly carries 120000 against a measured 28.35s cold start. Which number is defensible, on what tail-latency evidence — and is a static timeout the right mechanism at all versus a prewarm that makes the race unlosable?
